contract_sources.text: Hostile replacement of every authority file is outside this local integrity model. Production bootstrap/release is unavailable.
Accepted scope excludes hostile host authentication and production fixed owner/bootstrap.
Arbitrary coordinated rewriting of all trusted histories/anchors remains outside internal SHA-chain authentication claims.

not_claimed: Cryptographic owner/provider identity or anti-rollback authentication
Malicious-host-resistant accounting or irreversible terminal evidence
Live production authorization, authentic fees, real keys or full MODEL_CONTROLS
production_design_consequences: Before live release, explicitly name the trusted writer/store/identity and rollback boundary; no production fixed-owner acceptance follows from these fixtures.

If hostile local writers are in scope, use a separately controlled append-only authority or authenticated remote receipt/ledger with protected signing keys and rollback protection. A MAC whose key and counter are editable by the same actor is insufficient.

If trusted-host execution is the intended production assumption, document it precisely and independently validate admission/owner-wide budget/price/credential controls under that assumption rather than implying cryptographic authentication.
protected_boundary: The global fixture ledger assumes its retained billing evidence/event anchor are trusted together with execution code. SHA chains detect inconsistency, torn persistence and semantically invalid transitions; they do not authenticate the original provider reply against an actor who rewrites all billing/terminal evidence and reseals the anchor.
Keeping header/policy/context/quote/genesis unchanged does not preserve the replaced later billing/terminal authority.
Known-cost-undercharge remediation protects charges relative to retained known cost. It cannot prove an erased known-cost value after every retained copy is replaced consistently.
Same-ID/route/quote validation remains useful within trusted history, but a synthetic full legal transition history cannot be distinguished from actual provider history by local unkeyed hashes alone.
verdict: Both coordinated-authority replacement probes are accepted by the fixture implementation. This is a confirmed limit, not a new defect within the explicitly bounded accepted component contract. All cached real pilot owner/run files remained read-only.
